claims.text: Adding phosphorus to high-entropy or compositionally complex alloys will improve their glass-forming ability relative to otherwise comparable phosphorus-free alloys.
Adding phosphorus to high-entropy or compositionally complex alloys will improve the thermal stability of the amorphous state relative to otherwise comparable phosphorus-free alloys.
The proposed intervention applies to amorphous or partially crystalline high-entropy or compositionally complex alloys.
The effectiveness of phosphorus addition may depend on alloy composition.
The effectiveness of phosphorus addition may depend on processing route.
The effectiveness of phosphorus addition may depend on thermal-treatment history.
Phosphorus addition may change atomic structure, bonding, or defect formation.
Phosphorus may affect atomic diffusion, nucleation, or grain growth.
Improved glass-forming ability and amorphous-state thermal stability may enhance corrosion resistance.
